comments.note: The STRICT unresolved-marker regex in the test file (Group 7) is defined as a constant local to the test, not imported from build-personas.js. If the production regex mutates, the test will silently drift and continue passing against a stale pattern. Non-blocking since build-personas.js is integration-tested via --check --strict, but WP-002 (or a future housekeeping sweep) could export or co-locate the constant to close the gap.

module header comment in persona-helpers.js states the module contains 'All functions are side-effect-free ... except for the two file-name validators which call process.exit(1)'. process.exit is a global side-effect that makes the validators non-unit-testable without spying. The tests correctly spy on process.exit and restore mocks in afterEach — pattern is sound. WP-002 plans to unify validateCcFileName + validateVsFileName into a single validateFileName(persona, suite, field) which would be a natural opportunity to replace the process.exit side-effect with a thrown Error for cleaner testability, but that is out of scope here.

resolveConditionals() does not support nested {{#if}}...{{/if}} blocks (lazy regex stops at the first {{/if}}). This is pre-existing behavior from build-personas.js, tracked in the persona constraints documentation, and is correctly tested only for flat blocks. No regression introduced — noting for awareness.
No observations — code is clean and consistent with the project's CJS conventions. The extraction is conservative and surgical: no behavioral changes, no scope creep, no over-abstraction.
